content:
Below is a cautious, line-by-line rendering. Square brackets mark broken/restored text; **X** marks an unreadable or unknown sign; several lines remain uncertain because of damage and rare words.

1. **“From the time the day dawned, the Day was fashioned from its place in Heaven-and-Earth.”**  
2. **“From the time the night fell, the Night was fashioned from its place in Heaven-and-Earth.”**  
3. **“From the time the year appeared, the year’s fate/ordering was decreed.”**  
4. **“The Anunna-gods were born.”**  
5. **“Lady Inana acquired/obtained the *NIR.PA* status/office.”** (exact sense of *NIR.PA* uncertain)  
6. **“Lady Inana was made manifest/active throughout heaven and earth.”** (verb uncertain)  
7. **“Lady Inana […] was made beautiful/complete and was born.”** (middle portion broken; verb uncertain)  
8. **“Its divine ‘mound’/foundation […] was bound/fastened to its …-shrine/city (unu?)…”** (heavily broken/uncertain)  
9. **“The god Šaršar made the reed-beds grow; the little gods lifted up the *du₂-lum* (offerings/bundles).”** (some nouns uncertain)  
10. **“The river-gods pounded (and worked); they heaped up its silt in piles.”**  
11. **“The storm-gods roared; with their breath they set their word/command in place.”**  
12. **“At that time, broad wisdom/understanding—(that) of the god Šaršar—was abundant.”** (structure somewhat uncertain)  
13. **“Enki—(though) in the Engur/Abzu, amid the marshy waters—(found that) the place was not yet fit to be a dwelling of the gods; its interior was not yet dark/settled.”** (last clause uncertain)  
14. **“He lay down on his bed, and the Holy/Pure one did not rise.”**  
15. **“The gods lamented; they kept calling out; they performed the ‘a-nir’ (a lament/dirge) rite.”** (exact ritual term uncertain)  
16. **“While the pure man lay down, he did not rise from his bed.”**  
17. **“Namma, the mother who bore Enlil, gave birth (for) the gods of Šaršar.”** (final affiliation uncertain)  
18. **“In tears, the gods brought (it/him) to her child.”**  
19. **“X … they put him to sleep … and … they made him … (again).”** (too broken to fix securely)  
20. **“[X] … was struck/affected … [… did not] rise.”** (too broken)  
21. **“O divine one (*dim3-me2-er*), your hands—hands that fashion and fashion—… they made its ‘throat/neck’ sweet/pleasant.”** (address and object uncertain)

If you can share the tablet/source (composition name, museum number, or a photo/score), I can tighten several of the uncertain verbs and the obscure terms (*NIR.PA*, *du₂-lum*, line 13’s final clause, etc.).
